recent_posts.title: Coding Adventure: Synthesizing Musical Instruments
recent_posts.summary: A hands-on coding exploration of synthesizing musical instruments from scratch using additive synthesis. Starting with basic sine wave generation, the project tackles floating-point precision issues, implements ADSR envelopes with Bezier curve editors, adds harmonic overtone control, builds a dynamic audio compressor, and implements equal-temperament tuning with logarithmic pitch spacing. A MIDI keyboard is integrated for velocity-sensitive input. The piano is approximated by analyzing real recordings via a spectrogram tool, extracting harmonic amplitudes and decay characteristics per note, then interpolating between keyframes. The session ends with experiments producing flute and marimba-like sounds, illustrating the breadth of additive synthesis.

recent_posts.title: Coding Adventure: Analyzing Audio
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of building an audio analysis tool using the Fourier transform and short-time Fourier transform (STFT) to create spectrograms. Explores fundamental audio concepts like frequency, amplitude, and phase, demonstrates how to decompose and reconstruct audio signals, addresses spectral leakage with windowing functions, and implements interactive visualization with painting capabilities to manipulate and synthesize speech patterns.

recent_posts.title: Bad Apple!! but it's a smoke simulation
Coding Adventure: Simulating Smoke
recent_posts.summary: A detailed walkthrough of building a grid-based fluid simulation for smoke effects, starting from Navier-Stokes equations and implementing pressure solving, velocity advection, and buoyancy. The project progresses from CPU-based calculations using Gauss-Seidel iteration to GPU-accelerated compute shaders with red-black Gauss-Seidel for parallel processing. Demonstrates realistic phenomena like vortex shedding around obstacles and explores creative applications including painting tools and temperature-based effects.

recent_posts.title: I Made a Game in 4 Days (for the GMTK jam)
Coding Adventure: Ray-Traced Glass and Caustics
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive tutorial on implementing glass materials and caustics in a ray tracer. Covers Snell's law for refraction, handling reflection and refraction splitting, adding glass coloration through absorption, creating frosted glass effects with surface roughness, and rendering caustics from curved surfaces. Also explores spectral rendering techniques to create realistic rainbows by modeling wavelength-dependent refraction indices. Includes practical demonstrations with 3D printed models and real-world comparisons.

recent_posts.title: Coding Adventure: Software Rasterizer
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive tutorial on building a software rasterizer from scratch, covering fundamental 3D graphics concepts including triangle rasterization, perspective projection, depth buffering, texture mapping with perspective correction, basic lighting, and triangle clipping. The implementation progresses from simple 2D triangle drawing to a complete 3D renderer capable of displaying textured models with proper depth testing and basic lighting effects.

recent_posts.title: Creating 256 Bytes of Memory (in a simulation)
recent_posts.summary: An exploration of building computer memory through simulation. The post discusses the construction of registers and memory cells, explaining the progression from simple 4-bit latches to a 256-byte memory module. Key differences between static and dynamic RAM are highlighted, along with considerations for clock synchronization in memory operations.

recent_posts.title: Simulating fluids on a planetary scale: Gravity, tides, and collisions
recent_posts.summary: The post details an experiment in applying a fluid simulation onto a planetary model. It explores adjusting the gravity based on each fluid particle's position relative to the planet’s center. The author discusses Newton's gravitational principles and implements them in the simulation. Challenges like managing gravitational forces, ensuring proper fluid collision with the spherical planet, and visualizing tides with varying gravitational influences are addressed. The author also experiments with multi-body systems and procedurally generated planetary terrains to visualize and manipulate water flow in real-time.

top_posts.title: Coding Adventure: Sound (and the Fourier Transform)
top_posts.summary: The post explores the basics of sound and the Fourier Transform through a coding project. It starts with an explanation of how sound is recorded and represented digitally, progresses through extracting and manipulating audio data from wave files, and culminates in visualizing and playing back audio signals using Unity. The author also delves into creating synthetic signals, understanding the Discrete Fourier Transform, and reconstructing original audio signals from their frequency components.
